correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the finite-horizon Bellman induction for arbitrary conditional next-wealth laws. At k=1 the affine bound from the mean touches only at the legal endpoints. For k>=2 and a=(L-1)z, the logarithmic derivative of V_(k-1)(u)/(u+a) has the sign of z(M/u)^(1/(k-1))-u for L>1, with opposite signs at small u and u=M, and a unique zero at u*=z(M/z)^(1/k). The line c(y+a) also dominates the terminal value for y<=0, so the mean gives Lzc for every conditional law, not merely binary bets. Equality forces support at -a and u*, and the mean fixes the two masses. Induction along the visited surviving history gives the exact value and uniqueness; the two-point construction stops within budget. For L=1 stopped nonnegative fair wealth gives x/M, attained immediately. Strict convexity of log(1+(exp(t)-1)/L) gives strict budget monotonicity; its quadratic coefficient is (L-1)/(2L^2), giving the displayed deficit. The unlimited supremum follows by bounding success by time N and taking the increasing union for each policy, together with finite-budget achievability. The frozen grid tests were inspected, not run or used as the universal proof.
